together.title: People type their details once
together.note: A forms tool, a directory and a calendar bought separately each keep their own list of people. Here they are parts of one website:
together.form: A member who is signed in and signs up for the picnic doesn't type their name and phone number again. The form already has them from the directory.
together.added: A detail the directory didn't have yet, such as a phone number, is added from what they type on the form. What it already has is left alone.
together.calendar: What a member signs up for shows on the calendar on their own phone.

saving.title: One plan in place of several subscriptions
saving.note: The website, the forms, the directory and the calendar are $49 a month together, or $490 a year, with no charge per person.
saving.paying: Type what you pay each month now, to compare
saving.private: Nothing you type here is sent to us. Don't count accounting, online giving or a newsletter service: yaks.app doesn't do those.

how.title: The office asks, and the change is made

start.name: It starts from the site you have
start.detail: Type your website's address above. The preview has what your site says: who you are, where and when, and what's coming up. It has the words but not the pictures, and you send those to the assistant afterward. A preview you don't keep is deleted after 7 days.

ask.name: You ask for changes by email or chat
ask.detail: Write the way you would to a person on staff: “Here are Tuesday's minutes. Please post them.” The assistant makes the change and writes back to say what it did.

online.name: It goes online at your own web address
online.detail: Until then only you can see the preview. When you are ready you choose a plan, and the assistant walks you through pointing your web address, like %{domain}, at the new site. It is the one technical step. Then the new site takes the old one's place there.

behind.title: We watch for mistakes and fix them
behind.note: The assistant is AI, and AI gets things wrong. This is what happens when it does.

broken.term: A broken page or form is recorded as it happens
broken.detail: When a page fails on a visitor's phone, or a form doesn't save, it is written down that moment. The assistant starts on it right away: it finds the cause, fixes it and puts the fix online. When you sign in, you see each one and what was done about it.

ours.term: When the fault is ours, we fix it
ours.detail: Sometimes the cause is our own software and not your site. We are told as it happens, and we fix it. The assistant can also report a problem to us on your behalf, and our answer comes back to you.

wrong.term: A wrong fact is put right by asking
wrong.detail: No software can know that a meeting date is wrong. Each time it changes something, the assistant tells you what it changed, so you can check it. Reply that it is wrong, and it is corrected.

back.term: Any change can be put back
back.detail: The last 20 versions of your site are kept, so you can ask for it as it was before a change. Sign-ups or directory entries changed or lost by mistake can be restored as they stood at any time in the last 30 days, and anything deleted stays in the trash for 30 days.

yours.term: The site and what is in it are yours
yours.detail: Ask for everything in it as a file or a spreadsheet whenever you like, or delete it. We never sell what is in it or share it with advertisers, as %{privacy} says. There is no contract. If you stop paying, the plan runs to the end of the month you paid for. After that nothing is deleted, and the site has the Free plan's limits, which don't include your own web address.

write.detail: yaks.app is made by Yak Shaving LLC, a small company in Sturgis, Michigan. Write to %{mail} and we answer. Support is by email.

cost.title: $49 a month for the whole organization
cost.note: This is the Pro plan. Paid by the year it is $490 a year. One price, however many people you have.
cost.asks: Your office asks by email or chat, and the change is made
cost.people: No charge per person: staff, members and visitors cost nothing extra
cost.ai: The AI assistant's work is included
cost.emails: 2,500 emails a month sent or received by your site, such as the list each Friday of who is coming to Saturday's food pantry shift
cost.limits: Tax is included, and the bill never grows by itself. If a very busy month uses up the AI work the plan includes, the assistant waits until the 1st, unless you choose to buy more, $10 at a time and paid in advance. Your site stays online either way. There are two smaller plans, Free and $9 a month, for a site that needs less. %{plans}, where the assistant is called your Operator.

space.term: A space is one address and everything in it.
space.detail: That's its apps, their data and its people. Each space has its own plan and its own limits, and what one space uses never counts against another.

first.term: Your first space is free, and you can join as many as you like.
first.detail: You can own one free space. Every other space you make is on the Plus plan or the Pro plan. Spaces other people invite you into never count toward yours. If you already own more than one free space, they all stay free.

owner.term: A space's owner pays for it, and members never do.
owner.detail: Only an owner can upgrade a space, change its plan or cancel it, from that space's settings. Editors and viewers never pay, and there's no charge for each person.

limit.term: At a limit, nothing is deleted.
limit.detail: Adding stops: a new app, more data or another email waits until the space has room or moves to a paid plan. The owner is told which limit the space reached and how to upgrade, and your assistant hears when a space nears one. Members keep using everything, and visitors are always served.

stop.term: If you stop paying, the space goes back to free.
stop.detail: A paid plan runs to the end of the month you paid for. Then the space has the free plan's limits again and stops taking payments. Its apps and data stay.

assistant.term: Your Claude or ChatGPT plan pays for your assistant, and yaks.app keeps what it makes online.
assistant.detail: Your assistant builds and changes your apps on your own subscription, and that never spends a space's AI use. A space's AI use is for the AI its apps use themselves, such as reading a photo or speaking, and for yaks.app's built-in builder.

tax.detail: Any sales tax or VAT is in the price. Nothing is added at checkout.

fee.detail: Stripe charges its own processing fees. How selling works is below.

data.name: App data %{note}
data.note: What your apps save, like entries, lists and settings.

files.name: Photos and files %{note}
files.note: Pictures and documents your apps keep.

visits.name: Visits a month %{note}
visits.note: Counted in request units: each request for a page or its data is one, and 20 live updates are one. Past it, visitors are still served and the owner is told.

emails.name: Emails a month %{note}
emails.note: Sent or received by your apps. Invitations don't count.

ai.name: AI use %{note}
ai.note: What models and voice cost, in your apps and in the built-in builder.

builds.name: Builds a month %{note}
builds.note: With yaks.app's built-in builder, for people without an assistant of their own. A build counts when it puts an app online.

compute.name: Compute time a month %{note}
compute.note: Time your sandbox runs commands, and compiling code at deploy.

sandboxes.name: Sandboxes at once %{note}
sandboxes.note: Each sandbox is a computer of its own.

mail.term: Mail to your apps always arrives.
mail.detail: At the email limit, only sending stops. The count starts again on the first day of each month.

invitations.term: Invitations are free, up to 50 an hour.
invitations.detail: Invite as many people as you like, on any plan. Invitations never count toward the month's emails, and one person may send 50 an hour.

guests.term: Visitors who aren't signed in have a per-minute pace.
guests.detail: Anyone not signed in can make up to 300 requests a minute for an app's data from one place, and past that is asked to wait a minute. You and the people in your space aren't counted.

open.term: Visitors to an open app keep a visitor's pace.
open.detail: On an app anyone with the link can add to, each visitor may send 30 changes a minute, 16 KB at a time, and upload files of up to 2 MB. A visitor changes only what they added. You and your editors aren't held to these limits.

selling.title: Sell from your apps on a paid plan
selling.note: Take payments on the Plus plan or the Pro plan. Connect your Stripe account to receive payments, and handle refunds and disputes there. %{terms}.

start.title: Start with a free space
start.note: You can move a space to a paid plan later, from that space.

head.title: Help
head.intro: Build, host and share web apps: say what you need, and yaks.app builds it. You can also build apps by asking Claude or ChatGPT. This page covers setup, sharing, exports, and support. For anything else, email %{email}.

jump.where: Where are my apps and data?

make.title: What can I make?
make.lead: yaks.app supports personal and shared web apps: a recipe box, garden diary, book club schedule, potluck signup sheet, running log, or birthday guestbook.
make.basic: Start with one or two sentences. Ask for a basic version first, then request changes as you use it.
make.installed: You can also ask %{said} If someone has published a suitable app, your assistant can install a copy in your space. That copy has its own URL and data store; installing it does not give the publisher access to your space.

says.made: has somebody already made one of these?

start.title: How do I start?
start.lead: %{sign-in} with your email. We send a six-digit code; yaks.app does not use passwords. You land on your own space, and the steps for Claude or ChatGPT are there. After connecting, ask your assistant to build an app.

ask.title: How do I request an app or a change?
ask.lead: Describe what you want in your own words: %{said} Your assistant builds the app and gives you its link.
ask.changes: Request changes the same way. %{newest} %{note} %{photos} You do not need to specify every detail before the first version is built.
ask.undo: To undo a change, ask to restore an earlier version. The last twenty versions are kept. Restoring one changes the app's files, not its saved data.

says.app: Could you make me a recipe box? Something I can share with my sister.
says.note: Let Ana leave a note on each one.

where.title: Where are my apps and data?
where.lead: Your apps are hosted under a name you choose. For example, a recipe box can use %{recipes}. Ask your assistant to choose which app opens at %{yours}. Visitors open the URL in a browser and do not need to install anything.
where.name: Your space starts with a name from your email address. Change it at any time in your space settings, or ask your assistant to move your space. Every app moves with it, and old links keep working until someone else takes the old name.
where.data: Each app stores its own recipes, notes, photos, and other data. Changes are available on any device. Ask your assistant %{said} to list your apps and their links.

who.title: Who can see them?
who.lead: Set access separately for each app. You can change it later. There are three options:

read.option: Anyone with the link can read it.
read.detail: %{option} This is the default. Only you and invited members can make changes.

write.option: Anyone with the link can write in it too.
write.detail: %{option} For a vote, a signup sheet, or guestbook. Visitors can contribute without signing in.

invited.option: Only you and the people you invite.
invited.detail: %{option} Other visitors cannot open the app.

who.tell: Tell your assistant which option to use: %{signup}, %{private}.

says.signup: let anyone sign up on the potluck list

invite.title: How do invitations work?
invite.lead: Tell your assistant who, and why: %{said} Ana receives an email with your note and a link to accept. Nothing is shared with them until they click it, signed in with the same email address. No prior account or installation is required.
invite.roles: Choose whether the person can edit, only view, or invite other people. Membership applies to every app under %{yours}, not to a single app. Invite only people who should have access to the whole space.
invite.remove: To remove access, ask %{said} They can still sign in to yaks.app, but they lose access to your space. Their previous contributions are not deleted.

says.invite: invite ana@example.com to the recipe box, and say it's for Saturday.

broken.title: What should I do when an app breaks?
broken.lead: Tell your assistant what you saw: %{said} You do not need to diagnose the problem first.
broken.errors: Apps record errors automatically. Your assistant receives those errors the next time you use it. You can also ask %{said} and ask it to make a fix.
broken.restore: If a recent change caused the problem, ask to restore an earlier version. Restoring app files does not change saved data.

says.photo: the photo on the pancakes won't load.
says.errors: are there any errors in the recipe box?

out.title: How do I export or delete an app?
out.lead: Ask your assistant to export the app: %{said} It can return the app's data as a list or spreadsheet and provide the app files.
out.delete: To delete it, ask %{said} Deleted apps stay in the trash for 30 days. You can restore them during that time; after 30 days, they are permanently erased.
out.account: To ask for a copy of everything we hold about you, or for your account to be closed, write to %{email}. The %{privacy} says what we keep and for how long.

says.export: give me everything in the recipe box as a file.

people.title: How do I contact support?
people.lead: Email %{email} for help from a person.
people.report: You can also ask your assistant to report a problem for you.

under.title: Where are the technical details?
under.lead: The %{docs} covers app data, files, sharing, invitations, errors, and the tools available to an assistant. Its %{technical} page covers hosting, data storage, limits, and current limitations.

top.title: Terms of service
top.intro: These terms govern your use of yaks.app. By signing in or using the site, you agree to them.

about.title: About us
about.address: Yak Shaving LLC%{br} 971 S Centerville Rd, #2009%{br} Sturgis, Michigan 49091%{br} United States

service.title: The service
service.hosts: yaks.app hosts small apps built for you by your own assistant: Claude, ChatGPT, or another assistant that supports the same connector. You ask for an app, your assistant builds it, and it runs at an address of yours.
service.new: yaks.app is a new, small service. Features will change, and some of them will break.

accounts.title: Accounts and sign-in
accounts.codes: You sign in with your email address, or a US mobile number, and a six-digit code we send to it. Anyone who can read your email or your texts can get into your account, so keep them secure. Anything done from your account is treated as done by you. If something looks wrong, email %{mail} and we'll help.
accounts.age: You must be old enough to enter into a contract where you live, and at least 13.

content.title: Your content
content.yours: The apps you make and everything you put in them are yours. We don't claim to own any of it. You give us permission to store it, copy it and show it to the people you've shared it with, as needed to host it.
content.responsible: You're responsible for what you and your guests put in an app, and for having the right to put it there. Don't use yaks.app for medical records, card numbers, or other information subject to strict legal requirements.

use.title: Acceptable use
use.lists: Our %{policy} lists what isn't allowed. It is part of these terms.

visibility.title: App visibility
visibility.setting: Every app has a setting for who may see it. Private means you and the people you've invited. Public means anyone with the link can read it. Open means anyone with the link can also write in it. You choose the setting and can change it at any time. People you've already sent a link to will still have it, so take care when making an app open.

fees.title: Fees and payment
fees.plans: We offer a free plan and a paid plan. The %{pricing} lists what each plan costs and includes. Stripe sells and charges for the paid plan, and we will never charge a card you haven't given us.
fees.cancel: You can cancel at any time, and the paid plan stays active until the end of the month you've paid for. Each plan includes the amounts listed on the pricing page. We may also set limits so that one person's use can't take the service down for everyone else.

invites.title: Invites
invites.code: Your invite page has a code for the people you'd like to bring to yaks.app. Each person who signs up with it and builds their first app gives your space one more free month of the Plus plan. If you already pay through Stripe, your next charge moves a month later instead.
invites.others: An invite is for somebody else. Inviting yourself, under another address or number, isn't allowed, and neither is making accounts to collect the free AI use a new person's first space comes with. We watch for both, and may take back what was gained that way or close the accounts involved.

selling.title: Selling on yaks.app
selling.merchant: Your apps can take payments. If yours does, %{merchant}, not us. You connect your own Stripe account, the charge is made on that account, your name appears on the customer's statement, and the money settles into your balance on your own payout schedule. You pay Stripe's processing fee out of it, and we take a fee per sale. The amount is on the %{pricing}.
selling.stripe: Payment processing services for sellers on yaks.app are provided by Stripe and are subject to the %{connected}, which includes the %{ssa} (collectively, the "Stripe Services Agreement"). By agreeing to these terms or continuing to sell on yaks.app, you agree to be bound by the Stripe Services Agreement, as the same might be modified by Stripe from time to time. As a condition of yaks.app enabling payment processing services through Stripe, you agree to provide yaks.app accurate and complete information about you and your business, and you authorize yaks.app to share it and transaction information related to your use of the payment processing services provided by Stripe.
selling.duties: As the merchant, you are also responsible for describing what you sell accurately and delivering it, answering your customers, issuing refunds, responding to chargebacks, and paying any tax you owe. You do this in your own Stripe dashboard, which holds the money and the records. We never see your bank details or your identity documents. Stripe collects and keeps those directly. We keep the order (what was bought, what it cost, and the buyer's email address) in your app's store.
selling.forbidden: %{lead} Our %{policy} applies to sales, and so does Stripe's list of %{restricted}, which your Stripe account is held to. In summary, and not as a complete list: nothing illegal where you or your buyer are located; no adult services or pornography; no gambling or games of chance played for money; no weapons, explosives or dangerous materials; no drugs, drug paraphernalia, marijuana, or unapproved pharmaceuticals or supplements sold on health claims; no counterfeits or anything else that infringes someone's copyright or trademark; no debt collection, debt settlement, credit repair or payday-style lending; no money transmission, cryptocurrency exchange, or buying or selling of financial instruments; no multi-level marketing, pyramid schemes, get-rich-quick offers, or sales based on promises you cannot keep; and nothing intended to deceive or exploit the person paying.
selling.why: These restrictions apply because a shop on yaks.app sells under our name as well as yours. We may stop a space from selling, and Stripe may close a connected account, each independently of the other. If we stop your space from selling, we will tell you why where we can.

buying.title: Buying on yaks.app
buying.seller: If you buy something from a yaks app, your contract is with the seller and not with us. We host the seller's shop and pass the payment along. The seller takes your payment and owes you what you bought, and refunds and complaints go to the seller. The seller's email address is on your receipt, and replying to the receipt reaches them. If that doesn't resolve the problem, email %{mail} and we will do what we can, but we are not the seller and cannot fulfill the sale on the seller's behalf.

texts.title: Text messages
texts.what: If you sign up or sign in with your mobile number, yaks.app texts you the sign-in codes you ask for. If you text yaks.app to sign up, or ask for texts on your space's Operator page, it also texts you your Operator's answers when you text it, and its alerts about your space and the apps you build, such as when it finishes a change, needs an answer from you, or something needs your attention. Message frequency varies. Message and data rates may apply.
texts.stop: Reply STOP to stop texts, or HELP for help. You can also stop them on the operator page, or email %{mail}. Carriers aren't liable for delayed or undelivered messages. You don't have to agree to texts to use yaks.app. How we handle your number is in the %{privacy}.

ending.title: Termination
ending.yours: You can stop using yaks.app at any time. Deleting an app deletes its data. To close your account entirely, email %{mail} and we'll remove what we hold, as described in the %{privacy}.
ending.ours: We may suspend or close an account that breaks the acceptable use policy, or when the law requires us to. Where we can, we'll tell you why and give you a chance to retrieve your content.

liability.title: Disclaimers and limitation of liability
liability.as-is: yaks.app is provided as is. We don't promise it will always be up, always be fast, or never lose anything, and we don't promise that an app your assistant writes will do what you hoped. Keep your own copy of anything you can't afford to lose.
liability.limit: To the extent the law allows, we aren't liable for lost data, lost profit, or anything we couldn't reasonably have foreseen, and our total liability is limited to what you've paid us in the past twelve months. Nothing in these terms limits rights that your local law does not allow us to exclude.

changes.title: Changes to these terms
changes.update: When we change these terms, we'll update this page and the date at the top. If a change matters to you, we'll also send you an email. If you keep using the site after a change, you accept the new terms.

law.title: Governing law
law.michigan: These terms are governed by the law of the State of Michigan in the United States, and any dispute belongs in the state or federal courts in Michigan, unless the law where you live requires otherwise, in which case that law applies.

contact.title: Contact
contact.reach: You can reach us at %{mail}. We read every message.

privacy.name: Privacy policy
privacy.title: Privacy policy · yaks.app
privacy.description: What yaks.app stores about you, where it lives, and who can see it.

top.title: Privacy policy
top.intro: We collect as little information as we can. This policy lists all of it.

about.title: About us
about.address: Yak Shaving LLC%{br} 971 S Centerville Rd, #2009%{br} Sturgis, Michigan 49091%{br} United States
about.questions: Send questions, corrections and deletion requests to %{mail}.

email.item: %{lead} We use it to sign you in, to send your code, and to let other people invite you to their apps. We don't show it to other people: an app shows a name, never an address.

called.item: %{lead} When you first sign in, we ask what you'd like to be called. If you skip the question, we use the part of your address before the @. That name appears beside what you write in an app other people can see.

session.item: %{lead} We set this cookie for everyone. It ties anything written without signing in (guest entries) to the browser that wrote it, and keeps you signed in. Signing in puts your name on that browser's guest entries across apps. Visitor counts never use this cookie. The %{cookies} has the details.

campaign.item: %{lead} If the link you followed to yaks.app carries campaign tags or an ad's click id, we keep them, and when you arrived, in a second cookie for ninety days, so a sign-up can be counted against the campaign that brought it. Our own counts of each step from the home page to signing up keep the campaign's name, never who took the step. The %{cookies} has the details.

variant.item: %{lead} We sometimes show different visitors different versions of our home page. A third cookie keeps the name of the version you saw for ninety days, so you see the same one next time, and our counts of each step keep that name, never who took the step. The %{cookies} has the details.

codes.item: %{lead} A code lasts ten minutes and allows five guesses. We never store the digits, only a one-way hash of them, so nobody reading our records can sign in as you.

content.item: %{lead} Everything you and the people you invited write (text, lists, photos and any other uploaded file), along with who wrote it and when.

apps.item: %{lead} The files your assistant writes to build them.

mail.lead: Email your apps send and receive.
mail.item: %{lead} An app can have its own email address, like %{address}. We keep anything sent to that address in the app, including the sender's address, the message and any attachments. Anything the app sends goes out under that address.

mobile.lead: Your mobile number, if you give one.
mobile.item: %{lead} You can sign in or sign up with a US mobile number instead of an email address, or give one on your space's Operator page. We text it the sign-in codes you ask for and, once you've agreed, your Operator's answers and its alerts about your space and the apps you build. We keep the number, the words you agreed to, and when you agreed, and never use them for marketing. Replying STOP, or stopping texts on that page, ends texts; the number stays with your account as a way to sign in until you ask us to remove it.

errors.item: %{lead} If a page or a request fails, we record the error message, where in the code it came from, the address being visited, and which version of the app was running. We send that report to your assistant so it can fix the problem. It isn't a record of what you were doing.

counts.item: %{lead} So you can see whether anyone is reading your app, we count each page it serves: which page, which country the request came from, which site linked to it, and whether the visitor was a person's browser, a search crawler or an AI assistant. We keep only the counts. They contain no address, name, cookie or user agent string, so they can't identify or track a visitor. We keep them for about three months, and only the app's own members can see them.

builder.lead: What you say to our builder.
builder.item: %{lead} If you have us build an app for you instead of using your own assistant, what you type goes to a model that reads and answers it. We keep the conversation with your space so you can continue it later.

feedback.item: %{lead} If you ask your assistant to report a problem or send us a request or comment, your words are emailed to us at %{mail} and added to the list where we track them. Your name, your email address, the space and app you were in, and the version that was running are included, so we can look into it and reply. We keep those reports.

uncollected.title: Information we don't collect
uncollected.none: We don't keep an advertising profile, a history of where else you've been, your location, or your contacts. We don't keep your card number either: Stripe sells and charges for the paid plan, your card goes to Stripe and never through us, and Stripe tells us only your plan and whether it's active. We don't sell anything to anyone, ever.

stored.title: Where information is stored
stored.cloudflare: All of it is on Cloudflare, which hosts yaks.app. Cloudflare's workers run the code, its storage holds each app's data and files, its network carries every request, its model answers you in the builder, and its containers are the sandboxes where your agent runs commands. Cloudflare handles this information on our behalf and keeps its own operational records of requests, as any host does. That network is worldwide, so your information may be stored in a different country from someone else's.

shared.title: Who we share information with
shared.companies: Besides Cloudflare, we share information with three other companies. %{stripe} sells the paid plan: we give Stripe your email address so it can bill you, and Stripe tells us whether the plan is active. %{telnyx} carries our text messages: when we text you, Telnyx receives your number and the message so it can deliver it, and nothing else. %{meta} runs our ads on Facebook and Instagram. If you came to yaks.app by clicking one of them, we tell Meta, from our servers, when you open a page of this site and when you sign up: the page's address, the time, the click id Meta put on the link, and your browser's IP address and user agent, which Meta needs to match the event to its ad. We tell Meta nothing about visits its ads didn't bring, and never your name, your email address or anything in your apps.
shared.texts: We don't share your mobile number or your agreement to receive texts with anyone else, and nobody uses them for marketing, including us.
shared.others: Apart from telling Meta about the visits its own ads brought, we don't share information with advertisers, data brokers or analytics companies. Feedback you send us reaches us by email, so it passes through the email providers between you and our inbox, as any email does.

buyers.title: Buyers
buyers.card: Some yaks apps sell things. When one does, the seller is the merchant, not us (see the %{terms}). Your card details go to %{stripe} on Stripe's own page and never touch this platform or the app. Neither we nor the seller ever see your card number.
buyers.order: We do see the order, and it goes to two places. %{seller} receives what you bought, what it cost, and the email address you gave at checkout, stored in the seller's app so the seller can send you what you bought. %{stripe} takes the payment and holds the record of it under the seller's account. We keep our copy of the order for as long as the seller keeps the app. Deleting the app deletes it, and the seller can delete a single order.
buyers.receipt: We use your email address only for the receipt the app sends you. We don't add you to a list, and we never sell your address.

sellers.title: Sellers
sellers.connect: When you connect a Stripe account, we send %{stripe} your email address and the name of your space. Stripe then asks you directly for your business details, your identity documents and your bank account. %{never} Stripe tells us three things, and we keep only those: the account's id, whether Stripe says you may take payments, and whether you finished Stripe's form.

email.title: Email
email.sending: We send sign-in codes and invitations through Cloudflare Email Sending. Those are the only emails we send you without your asking, and each one results from something you or another person did.
email.apps: Email from your apps and feedback you send us go through the same service.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.none: No advertising or analytics code runs on our pages. We count the steps people take from the home page to signing up, with the site and campaign that sent them but not who took them, and Cloudflare gives us the ordinary request counts any host sees. What Meta is told about visits its ads brought is above.

seen.title: Who can see your content
seen.setting: You set this for each app. Private means you and the members you invited. Public means anyone with the link can read it. Open means anyone with the link can also write in it. Anyone you invite can see what's in that app.
seen.assistant: Your assistant sees the apps you connected it to, and acts as you when it does. We look at the content of your apps only when you ask us for help, or when we have to in order to keep the service running or to comply with the law.

retention.title: Data retention
retention.account: We keep your information for as long as you have an account.
retention.apps: When you delete an app, it goes to the trash. It stops responding at its address immediately, and we keep its data and files for 30 days so you can restore it. After 30 days we erase its data, its files and everything else belonging to it, and this can't be undone. If you ask us to erase it immediately instead, we erase it right away and keep nothing.
retention.spaces: You can close a space by asking your assistant to delete it and confirming the link we email you, or by deleting it yourself while signed in. The same 30 days apply to the whole space. It stops responding at all of its addresses immediately, and we keep its apps, their saved data and files, and your conversation with our builder for 30 days so you can restore it. We also hold the space's address for you during those 30 days. After that, we erase everything and the address becomes available to others. If you ask for the space to be erased immediately instead, your assistant emails you a link for that too, and we erase it right away.
retention.closing: If you ask us to close your account, we remove everything else, including our record of you. Backups and server records expire on their own in the following weeks.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.ask: Email %{mail} to ask for a copy of what we hold, a correction, or deletion, and we'll do it. Depending on where you live, including the UK, the EU and California, the law may give you these rights formally. We honor these requests wherever you live.

children.title: Children
children.under: yaks.app isn't built for children, and it isn't for anyone under 13. If a child's information has ended up here, tell us and we'll remove it.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.update: If this policy changes, we'll update this page and the date at the top, and we'll email you if the change matters to you.

cookies.name: Cookies
cookies.title: Cookies · yaks.app
cookies.description: yaks.app sets a cookie so you stay signed in, and one more when a campaign link brought you.

head.title: Cookies
head.lead: yaks.app sets one cookie, a second one when an ad or a campaign link brought you, and a third when you open our home page. This page explains what they do.

session.title: The session cookie
session.use: We set %{cookie} when you use an app, on yaks.app and its subdomains. Before you sign in, it holds a signed identifier for the browser that writes, so you can keep editing what you wrote without signing in (guest entries). Signing in adds your identity and puts your name on those entries across the apps you wrote to. It expires after ninety days of inactivity, and using it renews it. We don't use it for visitor counts or advertising.
session.clear: If you clear it, you're signed out, and the browser loses access to any guest entries you haven't claimed by signing in. If you refuse it, you can't stay signed in or keep your guest identity between requests.

campaign.title: The campaign cookie
campaign.text: We set %{cookie} on yaks.app only when the link you followed carries campaign tags (%{tags} and the like) or an ad's click id (such as Meta's %{click}). It holds those tags, that id and when you arrived, and nothing else: no name, address or session. It lets us count which campaigns bring people who sign up, and tell the ad network whose ad you clicked that its click led to a visit or a sign-up (the %{privacy} says exactly what). It expires after ninety days, and a later campaign link replaces it. Clearing or refusing it changes nothing you can see.

home.title: The home page cookie
home.text: We sometimes show different visitors different versions of our home page, to learn which one explains yaks.app best. When you open one, we set %{cookie} on yaks.app. It holds the name of the version you saw, and nothing else: no name, address or session. It lets us show you the same version next time, and count how many visitors to each version went on to sign up. It expires after ninety days. Clearing or refusing it changes only which version of the home page you see.

other.title: Other cookies
other.text: We don't set third-party cookies, and no ad network's code runs on our pages. Cloudflare, which hosts yaks.app, may set its own cookie to tell people from bots. That cookie is a security measure and isn't used to build a profile of you. Our %{privacy} has more about what we collect.

apps.title: Apps on yaks.app
apps.text: Apps in a yaks.app space use the session cookie, and we set no other cookie for them.

acceptable-use.name: Acceptable use policy
acceptable-use.title: Acceptable use policy · yaks.app
acceptable-use.description: What you may not do on yaks.app.

head.title: Acceptable use policy
head.lead: This policy lists what you may not do on yaks.app.

prohibited.title: Prohibited uses
prohibited.law: Break the law, or use a yaks app to harm anyone.
prohibited.children: Post anything that sexualizes a child. We remove it, close the account and report it, without exception.
prohibited.harassment: Harass, threaten or campaign against people, including through an open app that anyone can write in.
prohibited.work: Post other people's work, writing or pictures without the right to do so.
prohibited.malware: Host malware, phishing pages, or anything impersonating a bank, a company or a person.
prohibited.bulk: Use invitations to send bulk email to people who didn't ask for it.
prohibited.probing: Try to access someone else's space, or probe the separation between spaces.
prohibited.abuse: Mine cryptocurrency, run a proxy or a botnet, or use yaks.app as storage for files no app serves.
prohibited.traffic: Send so much traffic that other people can't use the service.

enforcement.title: Enforcement
enforcement.text: We usually contact you first and ask about the problem. We remove clearly harmful content immediately and close the account. Where we can tell you why, we will.

reporting.title: Reporting violations
reporting.text: Email %{email} and tell us where the content is and what's wrong. We'll look at it the same day where we can.

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.text: This policy is part of our %{terms}.

style-guide.name: Style guide
style-guide.title: Style guide · yaks.app
style-guide.description: Reference for the yaks.app design tokens, components, layout, and writing style.

head.title: Style guide
head.lead: This page renders the shared tokens and components used across yaks.app. Use it to check a change against the rest of the site.

how-to.title: Using the system
how-to.note: No build step of ours, four declared layers — tokens, base, components, and sections. Later layers take precedence. Every part below is one of the @yaks/ui kit's, in its %{linen} theme and drawn by its %{pencil} skin: the deploy composes them as %{ui} (sheet-assets.ts names the parts the pages wear). %{site} adds the face and what only these pages paint. The management pages' %{pages} and the site's %{style} load both and lay out their pages. Follow these rules when adding a page or component:

existing.name: Use an existing part before writing new CSS.
existing.rule: %{name} A part a page lacks goes into the kit, drawn by pencil, with an example here. The available titles, notes, chips, buttons, fields, tabs, sidebars, bubbles, windows, cards, rows, forms, and prose styles are shown below, and the rules they follow are under One design language.

roles.name: Use colour roles, never a colour.
roles.rule: %{name} Write %{role}, never %{colour}. The theme gives each role a light and a dark paint; a colour written down follows neither.

variants.name: Implement variants with custom properties.
variants.rule: %{name} %{variant} sets %{fill} instead of repeating the component's padding and border.

layers.name: Keep page-specific layout in the sections layer.
layers.rule: %{name} Reusable UI belongs in the components layer; layout used in one place does not.

how-to.complete: When adding a component, add a working example here so this guide remains complete.

pencil.name: Draw in pencil on paper, and keep surfaces flat.
pencil.rule: %{name} A card, a button, a window and a linked chip are drawn: a graphite line around it with slightly rounded corners. A field is drawn the same way around a well: a fill a little darker than the paper, pressed in, and what is typed in it stays crisp. What can be pressed sits on a hatch, so a hatch always means a press. One grain of paper lies over every page.

selection.name: Make selection visible in the shape.
selection.rule: %{name} A selected tab joins its panel, a pressed button slides onto its hatch, and the current sidebar tab joins the page along its right edge. Keep these cues in shared components so they work consistently in light and dark themes.

narrow.name: Keep prose narrow.
narrow.rule: %{name} Articles, help, and legal pages use %{measure}. Use %{wide} only when a grid, preview, or comparison needs the extra width.

subject.name: Name the subject and the action.
subject.rule: %{name} Write “Claude builds the app” or “yaks.app hosts it,” not “it gets built” or “the idea comes to life.”

nouns.name: Use specific nouns.
nouns.rule: %{name} Name recipes, files, invitations, and links instead of “things,” “bits,” or “what you need.”

filler.name: Remove filler.
filler.rule: %{name} Cut phrases such as “a little something” and “brought to life.” State the feature, limit, or next step. Contractions and questions are fine when they help the reader.

actions.name: Use concrete actions for links and buttons.
actions.rule: %{name} “Connect Claude,” “View pricing,” and “Open the recipe box” tell people what happens next.

claims.name: Make only claims the product can guarantee.
claims.rule: %{name} Distinguish an app hosted by yaks.app from ownership of a domain, source code, or exported data.

language.title: One design language
language.note: Every page yaks.app draws, the dashboard's tabs and the site's own pages alike, is built from the same few parts in the same way. A person who learns one page has learned them all.

card.name: A card holds one thing.
card.rule: %{name} A connection, a plan, the people in a space, one app's visits: each is one %{card}. Cards stack one gap apart, and a run of cards that belong together sits under a %{group} heading.

head.name: A card's head says what it is and holds what acts on it.
head.rule: %{name} The head runs across the top: a mark, the title, its status, then its actions at the right. Disconnect, Restore, Manage billing and Connect go there, a size smaller than a form's button, so a head stays one line.

hierarchy.name: Hierarchy is four steps of type.
hierarchy.rule: %{name} The page title; a card's title at 1rem; what a thing says at %{small} or the body size; and what describes it (a hint, a status, a count, a date) at %{fine} in %{muted}. The mono face is only for what a person copies or types.

rows.name: Like things are rows.
rows.rule: %{name} The apps using a connection, the people in a space, the agents connected, the apps in the trash: %{rows} in a card, hairlines between them, each row's actions at its right.

field.name: A field sits under its label, never at the end of a sentence.
field.rule: %{name} Every field (%{field}) is its label, its control and its hint, on one left edge and at most 34rem wide, in a form or alone in a card. One field and its button share a line (%{line}); a longer form ends with its button. What only a few people change folds under %{advanced} (%{more}) with a sensible default already in place.

space.name: Space comes from the container.
space.rule: %{name} Cards, forms and rows set the gap between what they hold; nothing inside carries a margin of its own. A card's parts are .75rem apart, cards one gap, groups two.

overlap.name: Nothing overlaps at any width.
overlap.rule: %{name} A name too long for its column is cut with an ellipsis and keeps its whole text as a title; a number is never cut and never wraps; a row that runs out of room wraps its actions under it.

theme-roles.title: The theme
theme-roles.note: yaks.app wears %{linen}, a theme of the @yaks/ui kit: every colour a part reads is one of its roles, and each role is a light and a dark paint. Values reflect the selected theme.

page-paints.title: Page paints
page-paints.note: What only yaks.app's pages paint, and no theme names: the person's bubble, the assistant's, an embedded app's ground and a field's well. They are declared in %{site}, from the theme's roles where they can be.

type.title: Type
type.small: %{name} %{value} — captions, footers, and what a card says.
type.fine: %{name} %{value} — what describes a thing: a hint, a status, a count, a date.

space.title: Space and shape
space.measure: %{name} — the maximum width for prose: %{value} in this context.
space.wide-measure: %{name} — the maximum width for grids and previews: %{value}.
space.frame: %{side} and %{aside} add a sidebar before the reading column and a gutter after it, and %{rhythm} says how far apart the page's sections sit. A page kind sets all four on its %{body}, and the header, the page and the footer are framed by the sum.
space.shape: Shape is pencil and paper: the colour and weight of a drawn line, how round its corners are, and how far a button sits off its hatch.

components.title: Components

notes.lead: Introductory copy below a page title.
notes.body: Supporting copy at the page's body size.
notes.small: A caption, a footnote, a date.

components.about: Each reusable component appears beside its class name. Dashed borders mark examples and are not part of the component.

titles.hero: Build an app by asking Claude

chat.ask: Could you make me a recipe box?
chat.caption: A caption at the foot of the exchange.

said.long: Use %{q} for words a person says to an assistant. The element remains a quotation without CSS, and the background continues across line breaks: %{said}.
said.invite: invite ana@example.com to the recipe box, say it's for Saturday, and put the newest recipes first
said.short: Short ones sit in the line the same way: %{said}

window.heading: Our recipe box
window.note: A note on %{on}: “Taste for salt twice.”
window.title: Example app preview
window.preview: A working app appears inside this frame.

yak.note: One transparent drawing, in %{file}, serves both sizes. Square exports provide the favicon, home-screen icon, and future app-icon sizes.

prose.title: Cookies
prose.heading: What Prose styles
prose.text: Prose styles its named paragraphs, lists, links, %{code}, and addresses. Elements with a component class keep their component styles.

kit.title: The kit's parts
kit.note: Every @yaks/ui part these pages wear, in every variant, as the linen theme and the pencil skin draw it. The examples are the kit's own.

sections.title: Page-specific sections
sections.note: The sections layer contains layout used in one place. Do not reuse a section class as a general component.
sections.top: %{Top}, %{Top_Name} — the shared site header. It is as wide as the page under it: %{Top}, %{Page} and %{Foot} all read the frame the page asked for. The home page shows the yak in its hero instead of beside the site name.
sections.page: %{Page} — the centred reading column and the two slots beside it. A page kind on the %{body} says how wide it all is, by re-pointing %{measure}, %{side} and %{aside}, and how far apart its sections sit, with %{rhythm}. Pages that contain grids or previews may use %{wide}.
sections.home: %{Home} — the home page's frame, asked for on its %{body}.
sections.hello: %{Hello}, %{Hello_Copy}, %{Hello_Yak}, %{Hello_Ask}, %{Demo}, %{Demo_Title}, %{Demo_Slides}, %{Demo_Controls}, %{Demo_Dots}, %{Demo_Dot}, %{Demo_Step}, %{Demo_Pause} (the examples' carousel), %{Yours}, %{Yours_List}, %{Make}, %{Make_Intro}, %{Make_List}, %{Make_Card} (a %{Card} an app is), %{Make_Shot}, %{How}, %{Steps}, %{Step_Name}, %{Join}, %{Join_Doors} — home page sections and their layout elements. Pricing also uses %{Hello}, %{Yours}, and %{Join}; homepage-specific overrides stay under %{home}.
sections.guide: %{Guide} and its elements — layout for this reference page.
